chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, linked up through a chain of narrators to Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him),
that the Imam considered two forms of selling to be disliked: 'Throw and take' (buying without checking), without turning the goods over, and buying what you have not seen.

key_terms.اطْرَحْ وَخُذْ: throw and take (a type of sale without inspection)
key_terms.شَرَى مَا لَمْ تَرَهُ: buying what you have not seen

ai.seo_question: What are the two forms of sales considered disliked in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Baqir’s prohibition of 'Itrah wa khudh' (throw and take) and buying unseen goods, highlighting the early juristic concern with *gharar* (uncertainty) in commercial contracts. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on transparency and mutual consent, ensuring that buyers can verify the quality and existence of goods before finalizing the transaction to prevent disputes.
